audit_findings.title: Growth may be valued without the capital spending required to produce it
audit_findings.magnitude: $621m 2025 capex; $531m computed gap between $2,814.2m anchor OE and $2,283m operating cash flow after total capex
audit_findings.mechanism: Excluded growth capex and related financing costs can overstate anchor OE while forecast growth is capitalized through the DCF.
audit_findings.evidence: As part of our supply network strategy, we have invested and will continue to invest in improvements to our existing manufacturing facilities and in new manufacturing plants.
audit_findings.explanation: The $531m gap is demonstrated, but the amount representing improperly excluded recurring reinvestment is unresolved. If the full gap were removed, the computed bear value would fall about $14.64 per share to approximately $66.85 and the base value about $17.29 to approximately $78.26, enough to change the conclusion that market price is below the bear value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile all $621m of 2025 capex to the maintenance deduction, classify each excluded project, include capitalized interest and cloud implementation spending, and rerun OE and growth with required reinvestment charged consistently.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may not contain the current debt structure's full recurring interest cost
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum indicated shortfall $74m pre-tax or approximately $58.9m after tax, comparing $296m expected 2026 interest payments with $222m 2025 expensed interest at the 20.4% filed tax rate
audit_findings.mechanism: A run-rate after-tax interest shortfall would reduce equity-level OE; capitalized interest may also enter through the capex reconciliation.
audit_findings.evidence: Interest expense, net of capitalized interest, was $ 222 million, $ 225 million and $ 239 million for 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is possible rather than demonstrated. Even applying the full indicated $58.9m after-tax shortfall would reduce computed bear value by about $1.62 per share to $79.87 and base value by about $1.92 to $93.63. Both remain above the $75.81 market price, while the resulting buy-below value remains below it. First-half 2026 expensed and capitalized interest totaled $142m, also indicating a full-year burden near, rather than dramatically above, the filed $296m schedule.
audit_findings.action: Normalize OE using a full year of interest on the June 2026 debt, reconcile the $123m expensed and $19m capitalized during first-half 2026 to cash interest, and ensure capitalized interest is deducted exactly once.

audit_findings.title: All cash was added although part may be trapped or costly to distribute
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $1.676bn bridge exposure, equal to $3.89 per share; affected portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Restricted, operationally required, or tax-burdened cash should be reduced in the equity bridge rather than added at face value.
audit_findings.evidence: We currently have substantial operations in countries that have cash repatriation restrictions or exchange controls in place, including China, and, if we were to need to repatriate or convert such cash, these controls and restrictions may have a material adverse effect on our operating results and financial condition.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates repatriation restrictions but not that a particular amount is unavailable. As a concrete outer bound, removing the entire $1.676bn balance would lower bear value to about $77.60 and base value to about $91.66 per share, both still above $75.81; the buy-below level would remain below market. Any actual adjustment should be smaller than this full-balance test.
audit_findings.action: Obtain June 2026 cash and short-term investments by jurisdiction and entity, identify restricted and minimum operating balances, calculate distribution taxes and conversion costs, and rerun the bridge with distributable excess cash only.

audit_findings.title: The IRS exposure may exceed the amount already recognized in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $450m proposed additional tax excluding interest and penalties; specific recognized reserve and incremental unreserved exposure unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any probability-weighted loss not already charged through earnings is a senior claim that should reduce the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the additional tax liability, based on the income adjustment proposed by the IRS under the RAR, is approximately $ 450 million, excluding interest and penalties.
audit_findings.explanation: The proposed $450m assessment is filed, but it is not a demonstrated incremental valuation error because Zoetis has already accrued an undisclosed dispute-specific amount. Deducting the entire $450m would equal about $1.04 per share and would not by itself change the conclusion, but the record does not allocate the June 2026 $226m uncertain-tax liability or $60m of related interest and penalties to this dispute, and future unrecognized interest and penalties remain unquantified.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the dispute-specific tax, interest, and penalty reserve through June 2026; estimate the probability-weighted settlement; subtract only the amount not already reflected in OE or recorded liabilities; and rerun the bridge.

audit_findings.title: The latest-year anchor contains explicitly nonrecurring accelerated sales
audit_findings.magnitude: 2.5%-3.5% of reported fourth-quarter 2025 International segment sales; dollar OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Accelerated revenue, profit, tax, and working-capital effects can inflate the FY2025 OE anchor and every scenario grown from it.
audit_findings.evidence: International segment revenue was positively impacted by operational changes made in connection with the Expected Fiscal Year Alignment, leading to an approximate 2.5% to 3.5% increase in sales in the International segment in the reported fourth quarter 2025 due to an acceleration of the timing of sales into the reported fourth quarter of 2025, a trend that we do not expect to recur.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing distortion is demonstrated and management explicitly says it will not recur. Materiality is unresolved because fourth-quarter International sales, associated margin, collections, delayed December orders, and the effect of the subsequent retrospective fiscal-year recast are not quantified in the supplied record. The sales percentage alone does not establish the net change in owner earnings.
audit_findings.action: Quantify accelerated fourth-quarter sales and their gross profit, tax, receivables, inventory, and cash-collection effects; offset delayed December orders; obtain the recast FY2025 cash-flow data; and rerun from a normalized anchor.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition contingent consideration may be an omitted senior cash claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $100m disclosed maximum, equal to approximately $0.23 per share; June 2026 fair value unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Unpaid probability-weighted acquisition consideration belongs ahead of common equity in the bridge if it has not already reduced OE or another liability.
audit_findings.evidence: The purchase price included upfront cash consideration of $ 111 million, excluding $ 19 million of cash acquired, $ 5 million in cash withheld for customary post-closing adjustments, and contingent consideration up to $ 100 million based on the achievement of certain milestones.
audit_findings.explanation: An omitted obligation is not demonstrated, and the filing says its initial fair value was not material. Even deducting the full disclosed $100m maximum would reduce value by only about $0.23 per share, approximately 0.2%-0.3% of scenario equity values, which cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the June 2026 fair value and maximum remaining PetMedix and other contingent payments, trace amounts already recognized or paid, and deduct the unpaid probability-weighted balance only once.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $39m in FY2018 and $30m in FY2024; the FY2024 amount equals 1.1% of the $2,814.2m anchor and approximately $0.98 per base-case share if recurring and fully eligible
audit_findings.mechanism: Verified non-economic residual D&A would be added back to OE, increasing operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2018 $39.0m (12.7% of filed D&A); FY2024 $30.0m (6.0% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated conservative treatment, not an overstatement error. The supplied residuals are small relative to anchor OE and scenario values: adding back the full $30m FY2024 amount on a recurring basis would increase base value by only about $0.98 per share and would not change the investment conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Classify the residual D&A components from filed asset and depreciation disclosures and rerun only for amounts proven to be eligible non-economic add-backs.
